name: Discrete Papular Lichen Myxedematosus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Discrete Papular Lichen Myxedematosus Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of multiple discrete, waxy, firm, flesh-colored to erythematous papules localized primarily on the trunk and limbs
Histological evidence of dermal mucin deposition with fibroblast proliferation without thyroid disease
No evidence of systemic involvement or paraproteinemia
Normal thyroid function tests to exclude myxedema related to hypothyroidism
Absence of sclerodermoid changes differentiating from scleromyxedema

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic papular lesions with histopathological confirmation of mucin deposition and fibroblast proliferation, absence of systemic involvement and normal thyroid function
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic forms of lichen myxedematosus and thyroid-related myxedema.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Discrete waxy papules on trunk and extremities
searchTerms: waxy skin spots on trunk and limbs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dermal mucin deposition confirmed by biopsy
searchTerms: mucin buildup in skin confirmed by biopsy
gel-like substance deposits in skin tissue
firm skin bumps, flesh or red color
hard skin papules with normal or red color

common.symptomName: Absence of systemic symptoms such as fatigue or weight loss

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness adjacent to lesions
searchTerms: mild joint tightness adjacent to bumps

occasional.symptomName: Mild tenderness on palpation of papules

rare.symptomName: Paraproteinemia detected on serum protein electrophoresis

laboratory: Absence of monoclonal gammopathy on serum protein electrophoresis
Normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
imaging: Not typically required; imaging may be used to exclude systemic involvement
other: Skin biopsy showing mucin deposition and fibroblast proliferation without fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic involvement including neurological and cardiac symptoms
Histology showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate without mucin deposition
Diffuse skin thickening and non-pitting edema

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with systemic symptoms
Development of sclerodermoid changes or induration
Detection of paraproteinemia or systemic involvement
references: Rongioletti F, Rebora A. Updated classification of papular mucinosis, lichen myxedematosus, and scleromyxedema. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2001;44(2):273-281.
Wollina U. Localized lichen myxedematosus (papular mucinosis): clinical and histopathological features. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2017;31(1):e1-e3.
